title: TCS London Marathon – Abbott World Marathon Majors race profile
claims: The first London Marathon was held on 29 March 1981; more than 20,000 people wanted to run, 7,747 were accepted and 6,255 finished, led home jointly by Dick Beardsley (USA) and Inge Simonsen (NOR); Joyce Smith won the women's race.

The event has grown to more than 43,000 starters and finishers, is broadcast in more than 196 countries and watched by four to five million viewers in the UK via the BBC; elite runners compete for US$308,000 in prize money.

The Majors panel lists course records as: men 2:01:25 Kelvin Kiptum (KEN, 2023); women 2:16:16 Peres Jepchirchir (KEN, 2024); women's mixed 2:15:25 Paula Radcliffe (GBR, 2003); men's wheelchair 1:23:44 Marcel Hug (SUI, 2023); women's wheelchair 1:39:52 Manuela Schär (SUI, 2017).

The one millionth finisher crossed the line in 2016; runners have raised more than £1 billion for charities and the London Marathon Foundation has granted more than £100 million to more than 1,460 projects.
